claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys is governed by competition between grain-boundary migration and phase separation.
Formation of metastable phases can mediate the competition between grain-boundary migration and phase separation.
Alloy composition influences the competition between grain-boundary migration and phase separation.
Grain size influences the competition between grain-boundary migration and phase separation.
Optimizing composition and grain size improves structural and chemical stability relative to conventional high-entropy alloys without such optimization.
The improved structural and chemical stability produced by optimized composition and grain size results in enhanced mechanical properties.
The prediction is intended to apply between 500°C and 1000°C.
The prediction is intended to apply to grain sizes from 10 nm to 100 nm.
The prediction is intended to apply across varying ratios of principal elements.
Grain-boundary migration rates and phase-separation kinetics should correlate with improved structural and chemical stability.
Mechanical properties should be enhanced when composition and grain size are optimized.
